text: The next morning Helen went to Hagenzeele Third, a cemetery raised above the road, where row after row of black crosses stood in the raw, unfinished ground. <break time="0.8s" /> The place already held twenty one thousand dead, and as she stared at the endless crosses, she realized that she had no idea how to find Michael among them. <break time="0.8s" /> She wandered helplessly to the left and to the right among the rows, wondering by what guidance she would ever find her own. <break time="0.8s" /> Then she noticed a man kneeling behind a line of headstones, firming a young plant into the soft earth, and she went toward him to ask for help. <break time="0.8s" /> When she came near, the man rose from his work among the graves and asked her quietly, Who are you looking for. <break time="0.8s" /> Lieutenant Michael Turrell, my nephew, Helen answered slowly and word for word, exactly as she had said it countless times throughout her life. <break time="0.8s" /> The man looked at her with infinite compassion and said, Come with me, and I will show you where your son lies. <break time="0.8s" /> When Helen left the cemetery, she looked back and saw the man still bending over his young plants, and she went away, supposing him to be the gardener.
